future_iṭ: 7.2.35 admits iṭ before the relevant v-alādi ārdhadhātuka. The an-iṭ condition of 6.4.51 is then absent: ṇic is retained, with its inherited guṇa/ay history. Kāśikā 6.4.51 directly controls this with kārayitā/hārayitā.
blessing_lopa: The selected P blessing is an-iṭ and kit/ārdhadhātuka. 6.4.51 removes the ṇic vowel, leaving ghāt- before the blessing endings: ghātyāt. Lopa is not a command to erase the causative event or retained affix provenance.
host_boundary: The outer liṅ belongs to the sanādi-derived causative dhātu under 3.1.32. Bare han’s vadhyāt from PG282 is not substituted for the causative ghātyāt. Lexical ancestry for the inner-prefix operation is not a universal permission to run every han rule on the outer derived host.
conditional: Retain the complete qualified future-event-failure context inherited from PG275, including its upapada/attitude premise. The augment lies inside the two ordered preverbs; no past augment is added to blessing.
luṭ: Only the third-person endings receive the ḍā/rau/ras replacements of 2.4.85. All first/second persons keep the appropriate finite -tāsi/-tāsmi etc. history, as reviewed at PG276.
non_today_future: The periphrastic future retains its non-today premise under 3.3.15; simple future uses its own 3.3.13 request.
pada_and_sense: The PG283 P action-result condition and actual causation frame apply throughout. Neither an A-pada request nor the separate narrating-kamsavadha vārttika is silently admitted.
domain: Two result-qualified han hetumati-NIC P profiles, with ordered pra+ni or pari+ni and retained causative event frame. The simple han/ṣo grids are a separate 360-position domain; no narrative NIC or A-pada expansion.
observed_and_composed: The causative stem, action-result qualification and source distinctions are inherited from PG283. Kāśikā 6.4.51 explicitly contrasts an-iṭ lopa with the retained future kārayitā, and 7.2.35 supplies the v-alādi iṭ domain. The 36 bare NIC cells are comparisons; all 72 prefixed words remain source-backed written derivations under the declared lexical-membership policy, not 72 literal new attestations.
